name: bunadh beag na farraige
text: bunadh beag na farraige is an Irish phrase built from bunadh, meaning stock, family, or host, and na farraige, meaning of the sea. It serves as a collective name for the small marine folk of Gaelic tradition, the household of fairy beings thought to inhabit the waters around Ireland. Idiomatic translations render the phrase as the small people of the sea or the little people of the ocean, and MacKillop groups the term with its sibling entry boctogai, the single-word label for the same order of sea-fairies.

attributes.attribute: Irish collective name for the marine fairies, glossed as the wee folk of the sea and paired with boctogai.

okr.objective: Document the Irish phrase bunadh beag na farraige and its link to the boctogai sea-fairies as recorded by MacKillop.
key_results: Identifies the phrase as a collective Irish name for the marine fairies, rendered as the wee folk of the sea.
Cross-references boctogai as the parallel single-word entry for the same order of beings.
